🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never...).
- Put these adverbs in the correct place in a sentence.
- Use frequency expressions (once a week, every day, twice a month).
- Ask and answer "How often...?" questions.

🔍 Warm-up
How often do you play sport? Every day? Sometimes? Never? The little words that answer this question are called adverbs of frequency, and this lesson teaches you to use them correctly.

I. The adverbs of frequency
📘 Rule (vocabulary)
Adverbs of frequency tell us HOW OFTEN something happens. From the most often to the least often:
- always (100 percent)
- usually
- often
- sometimes
- occasionally
- rarely / seldom
- never (0 percent)

✏️ Worked examples
- I always brush my teeth in the morning.
- She usually walks to school.
- We often play football at the weekend.
- They sometimes watch TV after dinner.
- He never eats fast food.

👀 Note
"never" already carries a negative meaning, so the verb stays positive.
Wrong: I don't never eat meat. Right: I never eat meat.

II. Where to put the adverb
📘 Rule (position) — the most important part of this lesson
1. BEFORE the main verb.
- I always do my homework.
- She often reads books.
2. AFTER the verb "to be".
- He is always late.
- They are never tired.
3. Between the auxiliary and the main verb (in longer verb forms).
- I have never been to London.
- You should always tell the truth.

📏 Simple pattern
subject + adverb + main verb ...
subject + to be + adverb ...

✏️ Worked examples
- We usually have lunch at one o'clock.
- My father is sometimes busy in the evening.
- I can never remember his name.

🛠️ Method: placing the frequency adverb
Step 1 — Find the verb.
Step 2 — Is it the verb "to be" (am, is, are, was, were)? → put the adverb AFTER it.
Step 3 — Is it any other verb? → put the adverb BEFORE it.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Wrong position: I go always to school → I always go to school.
2. Adverb after "to be" ignored: He always is late → He is always late.
3. Double negative with never: She doesn't never help → She never helps.
4. Frequency adverb at the very end: I do my homework always → I always do my homework. (Note: sometimes and usually CAN go at the start or end for emphasis: Sometimes I stay at home.)

III. Frequency expressions
📘 Rule (longer expressions)
Besides single adverbs, we use expressions that give exact frequency. These usually go at the END (or beginning) of the sentence, not before the verb.
- once a day, twice a week, three times a month.
- every day, every morning, every Sunday, every year.
- on Mondays, at the weekend.

✏️ Worked examples
- I go to the gym twice a week.
- She visits her grandparents every Friday.
- We have English three times a week.
- They travel abroad once a year.

👀 Note
"once" = one time, "twice" = two times. From three onwards we say "three times, four times...".

IV. Asking about frequency
📏 Form
How often + do / does + subject + base verb ?
- How often do you play video games? — I sometimes play, about twice a week.
- How often does he go swimming? — He always goes on Saturdays.

🛠️ Method: answering "How often...?"
Step 1 — Choose an adverb (always, usually, sometimes, never) OR an expression (twice a week).
Step 2 — Build a normal sentence with the adverb in the right position.
Example: How often do you read? — I often read; I read every evening.

✏️ Worked paragraph
My name is Salma. I always get up early because I usually walk to school. I often study in the library after class. I sometimes play basketball with my friends, about twice a week. I rarely watch television, and I never go to bed late on school nights. Every weekend I visit my grandmother.

⚠️ More common mistakes
1. Confusing "How often" (frequency) with "How much / How many" (quantity).
2. Putting exact expressions before the verb: I twice a week play → I play twice a week.
3. Forgetting the -s on the main verb in third person: She always go → She always goes.

⭐ Recap
- Adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never.
- They go BEFORE the main verb but AFTER the verb "to be".
- "never" is already negative; do not add another negative.
- Frequency expressions (once a week, every day) go at the end or beginning.
- Ask about frequency with "How often...?".

📘 Language bank
Adverbs: always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, seldom, never.
Expressions: once a day, twice a week, three times a month, every morning, every weekend, on Fridays.
Useful sentences: I always do my homework. / She is never late. / We play football twice a week. / How often do you read? / He usually goes to bed at ten.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Put the adverb in the correct place.
1. I do my homework. (always)
2. She is late for school. (never)
3. We go to the cinema. (sometimes)
4. They are tired after football. (usually)
5. He helps his mother. (often)

Exercise 2 — Complete with a suitable adverb or expression.
1. I brush my teeth ______ , every morning and every evening. (100 percent)
2. She goes to the gym ______ a week. (two times)
3. We ______ eat fast food; it is not healthy. (0 percent)
4. He is ______ busy on Sundays. (from time to time)

Exercise 3 — Answer with "How often...?".
1. How often do you read books?
2. How often do you play sport?
3. How often do you watch television?

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. I always do my homework. 2. She is never late for school. 3. We sometimes go to the cinema. 4. They are usually tired after football. 5. He often helps his mother.
Exercise 2: 1. always 2. twice 3. never 4. sometimes.

🗣️ Speaking task
Make a class survey. Ask three classmates "How often do you...?" about different activities. Report your results: "Amine always plays football. Sara sometimes reads."

👀 Extra note
The position rule is the heart of this lesson:
- Before the main verb: I ALWAYS study.
- After the verb "to be": She is ALWAYS late.
And never add another negative to "never": say "I never eat meat", not "I don't never eat meat".

📋 Summary
- Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, never) say how often something happens, from 100% to 0%.
- Position rule: BEFORE the main verb (I always go) but AFTER the verb "to be" (She is always late).
- "never" is already negative — never add another negative word (say "I never eat meat", not "I don't never eat meat").
- Frequency expressions (once a day, twice a week, every Sunday) usually go at the end (or start) of the sentence, not before the verb.
- Ask about frequency with "How often...?" and answer with an adverb or an expression.
- Remember the third person -s after the adverb: "She always goes" (not "go").
- "once" = one time, "twice" = two times; from three onwards say "three times, four times...".

enonce.question: Order (most to least): never, always, sometimes, often.
Place the adverb with "be": She (often) is late.
Complete: We ___ (usually) have lunch at noon.
Place the adverb: I (always) get up early.
Correct: I go always to school by bus.
Complete: They ___ (0%) eat meat (they are vegetarians).
Ask about frequency: (you / go) to the cinema?
Rewrite with an adverb: I watch TV every day.
Write a sentence about your routine with an adverb of frequency.
